notes:
Twelve numbered bullets and only one of them is not an action: [6] is the route through Castle Oztroja and folds into the fishing step. The ladder is a shuttle -- Ailbeche, Exoroche, Ailbeche, Ailbeche again, Castle Oztroja, Ailbeche, Selbina, Ailbeche, Exoroche, Trion's door -- and the page's own warning under [4] is exactly why steps 1 to 3 are kept as rungs: skip those conversations and you spend the Giant Shell Bug that the fishing step needs.

The one deliberate omission is evidence on the fishing step. Holding an Odontotyrannus looks like perfect evidence, and the page tells you twice that it is not. Sub-bullet three of [7] says you may fish it up BEFORE trading Ailbeche the bug, and [7] itself says the fish can be sent to other characters on the same account. Either way, holding one proves nothing about the rungs before it, so the only evidence in this quest is the Knight's boots key item Zaldon hands over at step 8 -- granted there, and listed in Item Reqs rather than in Reward.

Bullets [8] and [9] both trade 'the Odontotyrannus' and Item Reqs lists exactly one, so Ailbeche evidently gives it back; nothing on the page says to fish a second one up, and both trades are recorded as written. The rod is a real requirement that items cannot hold alongside the bait -- three different rods are named as working, and the choice is a genuine OR -- so the fishing step is items_partial with the names in its note. Step 11 is Trion's DOOR, not Prince Trion: the page says to select the door, and Door: Prince Royal's Rm is a real markable entity, so the reward step keeps a marker.

ADVERSARY (stage D): Dreadbug was removed from step 4's mobs. One step has one zone, and this one is the trade in Northern San d'Oria; Dreadbug lives in Crawler's Nest and is only one of the two ways bullet [4] gives for sourcing the bug, so he is a precondition, not a target of this rung. His location survives in the note. Everything else was attacked and stands: Knight's boots are granted at step 8 by the sentence that describes step 8, they are in Item Reqs and not in Reward, no item is evidence on two steps, the twelve bullets are in the page's own order, and the decision to withhold Odontotyrannus as evidence is exactly right given bullet [7] says it may be fished before step 4 and mailed between characters.

notes:
Seven bullets, all seven of them actions, plus an 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section of which nothing is a step -- party size, a 30 minute limit, one reward at a time, a once-per-Earth-day repeat, and the fact that a repeat only needs a fresh Moon bauble. The last two are recorded on the closing step. The unnumbered Trust warning above bullet [1] is a warning, not a step.

Step 2 is the Waking the Beast problem again: the page says only 'battle the six avatar primes' and never names one of them, never names the NPCs who grant access, and never names the six zones. Supplying Ifrit and Shiva from general knowledge would be exactly the guessing this rebuild exists to avoid, so the step carries no mobs, no zone and no target, and leans entirely on its evidence -- the six whispers, which ARE named, in Item Reqs, and all six resolve. That makes a strong rung: holding all six is precisely 'the six battles are done'. It also behaves correctly for a player who already had whispers from the Trial quests, since the ladder then sits on the hand-in, which is where they should go.

The fountain cannot be marked. 'Full Moon Fountain' resolves as a zone but is in the object deny-list as an entity name, and bullet [5] calls the thing you interact with only 'the fountain', so step 5 keeps its rung and loses its marker. That is the honest outcome rather than a name invented to fill the slot. The header's start zone 'Windurst Waters South' is half of zone 238 and is recorded as Windurst Waters.

ADVERSARY (stage D): step 5 was carrying target {object, 'Full Moon Fountain'} while its own note conceded the page calls the thing only 'the fountain'. A name the page does not give to the entity is an invented name however harmless it looks, so the target is nulled; the zone-level name on step 4 is untouched because bullet [4] does write 'Head to Full Moon Fountain'. The rest survived the attack: the six whispers are collected at step 2 by the sentence that IS step 2, the Moon bauble at step 3 and the Whisper of the moon at step 6, each granted at its own rung, none repeated, and none of them appearing in Reward.

you choose one reward, and only one at any time. Repeatable once per Earth day, and a repeat only needs a fresh Moon bauble from him -- the whispers do not have to be earned again.

notes:
Fourteen bullets and only four actions. [3] is a time limit. [6] to [9] are the conditions under which each of the three treasure chests appears -- [7], [8] and [9] are literally numbered '1):', '2):' and '3):' as list entries, not instructions. [10] and [11] are kite-and-burn tactics, [12] is the outcome of the fight, and [13] and [14] under 'Notes:' are the reward table. All of that folds into notes on the fight step; scanning for verbs would have produced eight steps out of it.

There is no hand-in. The quest pays out in chests that spawn on the boat once both NMs are dead, and the page never sends you back to Halshaob, so the ladder ends on the fight rather than inventing a return trip. Nothing here is observable either: the Imperial Mythril Piece is spent at step 1 and no key item is ever granted, so every step's evidence is null. For a single-battle quest that is the correct answer, not a gap.

Fame reads 'Treasures of Aht Urhgan', the expansion's name rather than a region, but it resolves to the Aht Urhgan fame area and that is plainly what is meant; the raw string is kept and it is flagged. The page never says the Cutter is clicked, only to head to it and that the battle then has a limit, so step 2 is recorded as an arrival in the manner of a cutscene-on-approach. Nor does the page say whether boarding changes zone, so Arrapago Reef is used for the deck, the imps and the cabin alike.

steps.note: once every 24 hours, which nothing in the packets reports

Dvucca Isle Staging Point out into Caedarva Mire, east to (G-9), zone into Arrapago Reef, then north to (H-8). The Caedarva Mire Survival Guide lands on the north side, a short run to (G-8), and an Arrapago Ring bought for 100 Imperial standing accolades teleports you in front of the Cutter. The page says only to head to it, never to click it, so this is recorded as arrival. Thirty minute limit once the battle begins.
two Windjammer Imps stand between the deck and the cabin. Killing them is not demanded, but for the third chest they must be ATTACKED rather than allowed to aggro, and they build TP for the NM fight.

both NMs are in the cabin. Kabsalah is a Corsair who always follows Wild Card with a weapon skill and double-attacks almost every swing; Bubbly is his Opo-opo pet with a heavy AoE Spinning Claw. The usual plan is to kite Kabsalah while the party kills Bubbly, then burn him. Up to three chests spawn afterwards: one for beating Kabsalah, one for beating him after Bubbly, one for surprising him -- pull him with spells or ranged attacks without alarming Bubbly, having attacked rather than aggroed the imps and kept him from hearing their flute abilities. He says something when surprised. The reward comes out of those chests; there is no hand-in.

notes:
Four bullets, of which [3] is an outcome -- the new weapon skill appearing in your list -- and not an action, leaving a three-rung ladder: cutscene, grind, hand back. The middle rung is the whole quest and none of it is visible to the addon: 250 Weapon Skill Points at 5 to 11 points a weapon skill depending on skillchain level, with no packet reporting the running total. It is kept as a step anyway, because dropping it would snap the marker back onto Zalsuhm the moment the opening cutscene ended.

The requirement is a Vigil Weapon EQUIPPED, and 'Vigil Weapon' is a class of weapons -- one per job -- not an item name. It does not resolve, so items stays empty on all three steps and items_partial carries the fact rather than a guessed weapon name being written in.

The wikitable of skillchain level against trial points was not converted by the prepass and sits inside bullet [2] as raw wikitext; its four rows are transcribed into that step's note so nothing is lost. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is all commentary -- the four progress-hint lines, the Ghanraam reset, and version history -- and contains no steps.

The job gate is the judgement call here and is why this is medium. The header states no job requirement at all, but the quest's own DAT name is 'Unlocking a Myth (Puppetmaster)' and it is one of a family of per-job quests, each unlocking one job's mythic weapon skill, so jobs is set to PUP. Gating it wrongly hides it from a Puppetmaster; leaving jobs empty offers it to every job in the game, which is the worse error. Flagged so a human can overrule it.

VIGIL WEAPON PINNED. The page says only "a Vigil Weapon equipped" and never names it, so the reading pass was right to leave it unresolvable -- 'Vigil Weapon' is a wiki CATEGORY, not an item. The job -> weapon mapping lives on Category:Vigil_Weapons, which is not in the scrape; it was fetched once and recorded in bgwiki-rest-cache/supplemental/vigil_weapons.json. This job's weapon is a real item with a real id, so the requirement is now checkable. Caveat kept honest: the quest wants it EQUIPPED and the addon can only see that you HOLD it, which is the near-miss direction -- you are one keystroke from ready rather than being told you are ready when you are not. | CORRECTED provenance: this page is reached through the redirect 'Unlocking a Myth (Puppetmaster)'. The record previously cited the STUB's page id and revision, whose content is a single #REDIRECT line -- not the wikitext the ladder was read from. It now cites the article.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 1: 'Vigil Weapon' names a class of weapons rather than an item and resolves to nothing, so items is empty and items_partial records the unexpressed requirement.

with the same Vigil weapon in the MAIN hand, kill things that give experience -- Incredibly Easy Prey or better -- and use weapon skills and skillchains until 250 Weapon Skill Points have accumulated. The page's table: no skillchain 5, level 1 skillchain 7, level 2 skillchain 9, level 3 skillchain 11. Weapon skills used before the quest was started do not count, and storing the weapon with Ghanraam in Aht Urhgan Whitegate (K-10) resets the total. Nothing observable reports the count, and bullet [3] is the outcome of reaching it, not an action.

trade him the Vigil Weapon; he unlocks the weapon skill for any weapon of that type and hands the Vigil Weapon straight back. Trading it early only earns one of four progress hints, which is commentary rather than a rung.

notes:
The quest starts on an unnumbered sentence sitting above bullet [1] -- 'Travel to the Durable Shields shop and speak with Guslam located at (H-8) on Warrior to begin the quest' -- so step 1 carries an empty source_bullets rather than pointing at a bullet it did not come from.

The coffer step is the good one. The header's 'Eld. Coffer Key -OR- Thief's Tools' is a real, expressible branch, so the key goes in items and the tools in items_alt instead of both being flattened into items_partial, and the Old gauntlets key item the coffer gives is that step's evidence. Bullets [1], [2] and [3] are one action between them -- go, open, receive -- and their sub-bullets are route advice: the Magicked astrolabe from Churano-Shurano, the northwest-of-map-2 ledge reached through Beaucedine Glacier, and the Lycopodium shortcut in Batallia Downs (S). None of those is a step.

Steps 4 and 5 are the page's own conditional -- 'If this is your first time completing a Borghertz's Hands quest for any job' -- so both are optional. The 1,000 gil traded to Yin Pocanakhu is not an inventory item and cannot be listed, hence items_partial there.

Bullet [10] holds two actions, Dark Spark dying and a torch being examined for the Shadow flames, and is split.

ADVERSARY (stage D): the draft singularised 'one of the torches' into a target named Torch on steps 7 and 9, on the reasoning that a wrong guess costs nothing. That is precisely the case hard rule 1 forbids -- the page writes the word lower case and plural and 'Torch' appears nowhere in its text -- and a guess that happens to collide with some other entity costs a marker in the wrong place. Both targets are nulled to {none, null}; both rungs keep their zone, grid, mobs and the Shadow flames evidence, so the ladder is unchanged. Nothing else was altered: the header's own OR is a real expressible branch, Old gauntlets and Shadow flames are each evidence on exactly one step and neither is the Reward, the first-time-only pair at steps 4 and 5 are correctly optional and correctly split across Upper and Lower Jeuno, and the Two Additional Coffers section is correctly not steps because the page says outright it is not required.

'Repeatable: af' is the artifact-armour category leaking into the field and means false. The Quest Req is that The Talekeeper's Truth be STARTED, not completed, which prev cannot express. The 'After the walkthrough: Two Additional Coffers' section is deliberately not steps: the page states outright that the Crawlers' Nest and Castle Zvahl Baileys coffers are not required and that the quest is complete once you have the hands.

  step 6: A ??? can never carry a marker; the rung is kept because the zone and grid are still worth having.
